security_audit.summary: The static backtick and hardcoded URL findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documentation links, and examples. The remaining material risk is the intended use of a broad belt CLI allowlist with external search, extraction, and LLM providers. No prompt injection attempt or malicious instruction was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Narrow allowed-tools from Bash(belt *) to the specific Tavily and Exa commands required by this skill.
Warn users before sending secrets, private URLs, proprietary content, or sensitive prompts to external providers.
Prefer pinned installation documentation or checksummed release instructions instead of a mutable raw branch URL.

content.value_statement: Finding current web evidence can slow down research and agent workflows. This skill runs Tavily and Exa searches through belt for sourced answers and extracted content.
actual_capabilities: Runs Tavily Search Assistant through the belt CLI for web questions.
Extracts readable text and images from URLs with Tavily Extract.
Runs Exa Search, Exa Answer, and Exa Extract workflows.
Supports research pipelines that save search or extraction output for later analysis.
Shows how to combine search results with Claude models through OpenRouter apps.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI to be installed and authenticated.
Sends queries, URLs, and extracted content to external service providers.
Depends on provider availability, account permissions, and network access.
Does not independently verify the trustworthiness of returned sources.

use_cases.title: Current Topic Research
use_cases.description: Search recent web sources and collect links, answers, and page context for a research question.

use_cases.title: RAG Source Collection
use_cases.description: Find and extract pages that can support a retrieval-augmented generation workflow.

use_cases.title: Claim Verification
use_cases.description: Compare search results and source pages before accepting a factual claim.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Web Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the web for recent information about [topic] using Tavily. Return the answer, source links, and useful images.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Page Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract readable content from these URLs: [urls]. Summarize the key points and list the source pages.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Run both Tavily and Exa searches for [query]. Compare the top results, source quality, and conflicting claims.

prompt_templates.title: Build Research Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for [topic], extract the most relevant pages, then summarize trends with Claude. Keep source citations separate from analysis.

output_examples.input: Search for recent advances in battery recycling.
output_examples.output: A concise answer with source links, publication context, and notes on which results appear most relevant.

output_examples.input: Extract and summarize three product documentation pages.
output_examples.output: Clean page summaries, key images when available, and a source list for follow-up review.

output_examples.input: Compare Tavily and Exa results for a market research question.
output_examples.output: A provider comparison that highlights overlapping sources, unique results, and claims that need verification.

best_practices: Use precise queries and ask for source links with every answer.
Review extracted pages before using their content in reports or agents.
Remove secrets and private identifiers before sending prompts or URLs to providers.
anti_patterns: Do not treat search summaries as verified facts without source review.
Do not send confidential documents or private URLs through external extraction tools.
Do not use broad research prompts when a narrow query would reduce irrelevant results.

faq.question: What services does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses Tavily and Exa apps through the inference.sh belt CLI.

faq.question: Does it require an account?
faq.answer: Yes. The belt CLI must be installed, and users must sign in before running app commands.

faq.question: Can it extract content from any page?
faq.answer: No. Extraction depends on provider access, page availability, robots rules, and account limits.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive data?
faq.answer: Use caution. Queries, URLs, and extracted content may be sent to external providers.

faq.question: Can it support RAG workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It can collect and extract source pages for later retrieval or summarization workflows.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
